in_text_mentions: due to the weakness of the flexor muscles of the leg and foot on the left side. Ocular movement was restricted on right lateral gaze. The patient’s eye lid was swollen, tender and fluctuant on palpation. Diagnostic nasal endoscopy (DNE) revealed bulging of the right lateral wall of the nose and mucopurulent discharge in the middle meatus. Contrast enhanced computer tomography (CECT) of the nose and paranasal sinus demonstrated bilateral pan sinusitis with right subperiosteal abscess (Fig2).

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A, B, C, D). A: Histology of sinus tissue from the patient with COVID-19-associated acute rhinosinusitis showing multiple calcium oxalate crystals described in the caption as indicative of aspergillosis, the causative agent of the documented acute rhinosinusitis; no vocabulary finding key applies, so crystals are proposed. B: Same specimen as panel A with calcium oxalate crystals highlighted under low light, a recognized marker of Aspergillus-related acute rhinosinusitis in this patient; crystals are not in the vocabulary so they are proposed. C: Panel directly shows neutrophil-predominant (polymorphonuclear) inflammatory infiltrate in sinus tissue, matching the vocabulary finding for acute rhinosinusitis histology. D: Histology shows a degenerated hypha invading bone with calcium oxalate crystals in the maxillary sinus of the patient with acute rhinosinusitis; invasive fungal involvement is a complication of the documented sinus disease and the...

source_variants.context: Contrast CT shows an axial superior-medial subperiosteal abscess with a smaller rim-enhancing fluid collection below it, and coronal views showing mucosal thickening and air-fluid levels in the right maxillary, ethmoid, and sphenoid sinuses.
source_variants.context_summary: Contrast CT shows an axial superior-medial subperiosteal abscess with a smaller rim-enhancing fluid collection below it, and coronal views showing mucosal thickening and air-fluid levels in the right maxillary, ethmoid, and sphenoid sinuses.
source_variants.figure_caption: Computed tomography with contrast images of the presented case: (a) axial cut demonstrating a superior and medial subperiosteal abscess (yellow arrow). (b) a smaller rim-enhancing fluid collection inferior to the abscess in A. (c) & (d) coronal sections through the paranasal sinuses with notable mucosal thickening and mucosal thickening with air-fluid levels within the right maxillary sinus, right ethmoid air cells, and right sphenoid sinus.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (a, b). a: Coronal CT of the paranasal sinuses in a real patient showing opacification consistent with pansinusitis, directly captioned as sinusitis in the paranasal scan in a case report of acute rhinosinusitis.
